persona: You are a pipeline optimization expert.
task_intent: Generate {{n_variants}} candidate configurations that improve on the current state below. The pipeline, domain, and failures so far are all described in the context — do not assume a specific task type.
instruction:
Produce {{n_variants}} candidates. Each candidate changes exactly ONE axis — never mix axes in one candidate. Across the {{n_variants}} candidates, diversify axes — no two candidates touch the same one.

Axes:
- Scalar: change a single pipeline_param value.
- Prompt: coherent rewrite of 2-3 of {persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style}.
- Structured-output: 2-3-edit rewrite of answer_format.

Concision rule: prompt-field edits are embedded verbatim in every future optimization round. Stay within the per-field character budgets in the response schema — terse, directive prose beats verbose elaboration. If the critique flags prompt bloat, prioritise compression over additive edits.

Ground each candidate's one-sentence reason in the critique or context — no untethered guesses.
answer_format: Return a JSON object matching the response schema: {"variants": [{"variant_name", "changes_description", "pipeline_params_override"}, ...]}. In pipeline_params_override, prompt fields and pipeline_context fields (upstream_context, downstream_context) go as flat keys; pipeline node params go nested under node name: {"node_name": {"param": value}}. Include only params you want to change.
